services.title: House Framing
services.summary: Structural timber framing for new homes — wall frames, roof trusses, floor joists and load-bearing structure built to the National Construction Code.
services.lead: We deliver complete timber framing for Adelaide residential projects using compliant materials and precise workmanship, so the skeleton of your build is straight, solid and built to last.

sections.title: Wall frame construction
sections.summary: Load-bearing and non-load-bearing wall frames built to AS 1684 using H3/H4 treated timber, for single, double and split-level homes.

sections.title: Roof trusses & rafters
sections.summary: Prefabricated truss or site-cut rafter installation with weatherproof detailing and cyclone-rated fixing for full roof-structure integrity.

sections.title: Floor joist laying
sections.summary: Joists sized to span and load, on concrete slab or suspended floors, with moisture barrier and preservative treatment.

sections.title: Structural alignment
sections.summary: Laser-levelled checks throughout for plumb, level and dimensional accuracy within building tolerances.

sections.title: Reading the plans before timber arrives
sections.summary: A reliable frame starts with a complete set of current drawings. We review wall heights, openings, roof geometry, connection details and any engineer or truss documentation before work begins, then raise clashes early rather than leaving decisions to the day of installation. This gives builders and owners a clearer sequence for deliveries, trades and inspections.

sections.title: Set-out for openings and services
sections.summary: Doors, windows, stair voids, wet-area penetrations and service runs all affect the frame. We set out these points from the approved drawings, check rough opening dimensions and coordinate where plumbing, electrical or mechanical work needs allowance. Care at this stage helps prevent later cutting, packing and patching that can compromise the finish.

sections.title: Timber selection and site storage
sections.summary: The right member, treatment level and connection detail depend on its job and exposure. Timber is kept supported, protected from standing water and handled to limit unnecessary damage or twist before it is fixed. Where a design calls for proprietary components, we work to the supplier information and the project documentation rather than substituting by assumption.

sections.title: Installation sequence at lock-up
sections.summary: Framing is planned around access, lifting, bracing, truss installation and the next trade. We keep the work area orderly and communicate practical hold points so that survey, engineering or building inspections can occur without avoidable delay. The aim is a frame that is ready for roof, cladding and internal trades to follow efficiently.

sections.title: Checks before the next trade starts
sections.summary: Before handing an area forward, we visually review line, plumb, level, bracing, openings and obvious damage. MEL ONE identifies any work needed while it is accessible and discusses required inspections, engineering sign-off and the responsible project parties as part of the agreed framing scope.

sections.title: What to include in a framing enquiry
sections.summary: For a useful Adelaide framing discussion, provide current architectural and structural drawings, site address, access constraints, build stage, preferred start window and whether supply is included. Mention slopes, extensions tying into an existing home, unusual roof shapes or tight boundaries. Clear information lets us assess the real scope instead of offering a vague allowance.

services.title: Outdoor Living
services.summary: Custom outdoor spaces for Australian homes — treated timber decking, pergolas, fencing and coastal-grade landscape timber.
services.lead: Adelaide's coastal climate is hard on outdoor timber. We specify certified preservative-treated timber with proper drainage and fixing so your outdoor space stays looking new for years.

sections.title: Timber decking
sections.summary: Merbau, Spotted Gum or Treated Pine decks with vented sub-structure, drainage gaps and slip-resistant finish for homes, pools and commercial areas.

sections.title: Pergolas & shade structures
sections.summary: Freestanding or attached pergolas with weatherproof joints, steel connectors and treated hardwood, ready for motorised shade or greenery.

sections.title: Fencing
sections.summary: Termite-resistant treated timber fences, custom oiling and staining, with concrete footings and wind bracing for boundary and privacy needs.

sections.title: Coastal preservative timber
sections.summary: H4/H5 treated timber with stainless fixings and a maintenance plan for Adelaide's salt-air coastal suburbs.

sections.title: Start with how the space will be used
sections.summary: A deck for quiet meals, a pool edge, a shaded play zone and an entertaining area all need different layouts, circulation and finishes. We ask how many people use the space, where furniture and barbecue equipment will sit, how the house opens to the yard and what needs to remain accessible before proposing a board direction or structure.

sections.title: Levels, drainage and ground clearance
sections.summary: Outdoor timber lasts better when water can move away and air can circulate below it. We assess existing levels, thresholds, drainage paths, garden edges and access to subfloor areas so the finished deck does not create a practical water trap. Site conditions determine the appropriate substructure, footing approach and transitions to paving or lawn.

sections.title: Board, fixing and finish choices
sections.summary: Species, profile, colour, fasteners and coating should be chosen together, not as isolated showroom decisions. We explain the visual and maintenance implications of common timber options, exposed versus concealed fixing, and oil or coating systems. This helps clients balance initial appearance, barefoot comfort, future touch-ups and the character that real timber develops outdoors.

sections.title: Pergola and privacy integration
sections.summary: A pergola, screen or fence works best when it is designed with the deck rather than added after it. We consider shade direction, posts, fixings, privacy lines, lighting and the relationship to existing walls and services. Where approvals, engineering or boundary requirements apply, these need to be resolved through the appropriate project process before construction proceeds.

sections.title: A practical maintenance plan
sections.summary: Maintenance is easier when it is planned at handover. We can discuss cleaning, clearing leaves from gaps, watching for coating wear, keeping drainage paths open and checking high-exposure areas. The right interval depends on species, finish, sunlight, weather and use, so we avoid one-size-fits-all promises and focus on what the finished space actually needs.

sections.title: Preparing an outdoor-living brief
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the outdoor area, features and style you want. We measure the site and check access, levels and connections to the house before confirming design, preparation and the written quote. Existing photos, sketches and approximate dimensions are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available.

services.title: Fix-Out & Second Fix
services.summary: On-site finishing after lock-up — cornices, skirtings, door frames and leaves, window frames and timber stairs to a full building-fit standard.
services.lead: Second fix is the final quality gate before handover. With precise measuring and professional installation we make sure every detail lands perfectly.

sections.title: Cornices & mouldings
sections.summary: Cornice, ceiling cove, curtain boxes and custom plaster features, with stopper, sand and primer.

sections.title: Skirtings & architraves
sections.summary: Solid timber, MDF or composite skirtings and architraves, with accurate cutting, 45° mitres and nail-free fixing.

sections.title: Door frames & leaves
sections.summary: Internal, fire-rated and security doors — frame plumb, leaf hung and hardware set, with acoustic and sealing treatment.

sections.title: Timber stair installation
sections.summary: Treads, risers, balusters and handrails fitted and tuned on site for consistent step height and a straight rail.

sections.title: The right time for second-fix work
sections.summary: Second fix performs best when framing, linings, floor levels and service rough-ins are sufficiently complete and dry. Starting too early can lead to damaged trim, changed openings or repeated work. We coordinate with the builder or site manager about readiness, delivery timing, room-by-room access and protection of finished surfaces.

sections.title: Consistent reveals and junctions
sections.summary: The small lines around doors, windows, skirtings and built-ins are what make a room feel intentional. We measure from established reference points, account for floor finishes and check how trims meet at corners, stairs and cabinetry. This approach helps avoid visibly uneven reveals and awkward transitions that are expensive to correct after painting.

sections.title: Door operation and hardware coordination
sections.summary: A door can look correct and still perform poorly if clearances, hinges, seals, locks or strike plates are not coordinated. We check handing, swing, required hardware, finished floor level and adjacent cabinetry before final adjustment. Fire, acoustic, security or accessibility requirements should be identified in the approved project documentation before installation.

sections.title: Working with paint and flooring trades
sections.summary: Second-fix carpentry sits between several finishing trades. We plan sequencing with plaster, painting, flooring, glazing and cabinetry so joints are prepared appropriately and completed items are not damaged by later work. Straightforward communication about who owns caulking, filling, coating and touch-up prevents gaps in the final handover scope.

sections.title: Finish review before handover
sections.summary: Before an area is signed off, we review alignment, mitres, fixing points, movement, hardware operation and visible damage in normal viewing conditions. Any agreed defects are easier to manage while materials and access are still available. This trade review complements, rather than replaces, the builder's quality process and any required certification.

sections.title: Information that improves a second-fix quote
sections.summary: Provide the door and window schedules, interior elevations, trim profiles, hardware schedule, finish level, floor finish details and timing. For renovations, photos of existing openings and walls are valuable. These details let us allow for the actual junctions and installation conditions instead of treating a detailed finishing package as a simple linear-metre estimate.

services.title: Formwork Carpentry
services.summary: Precise timber formwork for commercial builds and large footings — accurate concrete shaping and safe site practice.
services.lead: Formwork is the foundation of concrete quality. We use careful set-out, a solid bracing system and strict inspection so large projects get a reliable timber form system.

sections.title: Foundation wall formwork
sections.summary: Suspended-slab, retaining-wall and beam formwork with damp-proof membrane and embedded-item fixing.

sections.title: Slab & beam formwork
sections.summary: Multi-level slab systems with Acrow props, primary and secondary bearers and accurately laid form face.

sections.title: Feature-shape formwork
sections.summary: Curved, raked and irregular concrete elements built in timber to match architect detail.

sections.title: Set-out before formwork is fabricated
sections.summary: Formwork begins with the current structural drawings, pour sequence and site set-out. We confirm dimensions, levels, penetrations, rebates, construction joints and access before cutting material. Early review is particularly important where multiple concrete elements meet, because a small error in one pour can affect the next trade and the visible finish.

sections.title: Temporary works and bracing coordination
sections.summary: Formwork is temporary, but it must be treated as a serious site system. The support, bracing, pour rate, access and stripping sequence are considered with the project team and relevant documentation. We work within the agreed temporary-works approach and escalate items requiring engineering or site management direction rather than improvising structural decisions.

sections.title: Embedded items and trade interfaces
sections.summary: Sleeves, bolts, starter bars, services and cast-in items need to be located before concrete is placed. We coordinate these interfaces against the issued information and identify clashes while adjustment is still possible. This reduces the risk of drilling, cutting or patching newly completed concrete because an item was missed or shifted at the last moment.

sections.title: Form-face quality and concrete finish
sections.summary: The selected form face, joints, ties and release process influence the appearance of exposed concrete. Where finish expectations are important, we discuss them early with the builder, concrete contractor and designer so the formwork system is matched to the specified result. Concrete placement and curing remain specialist activities coordinated through the wider construction team.

sections.title: Safe access and orderly stripping
sections.summary: Formwork operations need clear access, material handling space and a controlled removal sequence. We keep work areas organised and follow the agreed direction for inspection, pour readiness and stripping. No form is removed simply because it looks complete; timing and release must follow the project's engineering, program and site-safety requirements.

sections.title: Scoping commercial formwork accurately
sections.summary: Useful information includes structural drawings, details, concrete programme, finish requirements, elevation or slab levels, access and lifting constraints, and whether the scope is supply, erect, strip or a combination. Sharing this early helps identify the right system and labour sequence for the project rather than relying on a generic rate that does not reflect real site conditions.

services.title: Fitout & Refurbishment
services.summary: Timber partitions, feature ceilings and display walls for offices, restaurants and retail — full commercial carpentry.
services.lead: Commercial fitouts need speed and quality together. We work fast, build accurately and disturb trading as little as possible for Adelaide businesses.

sections.title: Timber partition systems
sections.summary: Steel-stud with timber-faced partitions, acoustic batts and finished surfaces, demountable for future re-layout.

sections.title: Feature & suspended ceilings
sections.summary: Commercial ceiling systems with hidden light coves, vents and fire-spray coordination, plus custom timber feature ceilings.

sections.title: Shopfront & display walls
sections.summary: Retail timber feature walls, brand displays and custom furniture with commercial-grade hard-wearing surfaces.

sections.title: Fitout planning around the operating business
sections.summary: An office, café, clinic or retail space has to keep functioning around deliveries, staff, customers and building rules. We begin by understanding the trading requirements, access hours, noisy-work restrictions, landlord process and opening date. That context informs a realistic carpentry sequence instead of assuming every commercial site can be treated like an empty shell.

sections.title: Reading drawings, finishes and brand intent
sections.summary: Commercial drawings often combine architectural, services, fire, joinery and signage information. We review the details relevant to our work, confirm visible finishes and identify interfaces before fabrication or site installation. This helps protect a designer's intent while keeping practical questions—such as service access, durability and cleanability—visible to the project team.

sections.title: Sequencing around services and approvals
sections.summary: Ceilings, partitions, feature linings and display elements must work around mechanical, electrical, hydraulic and fire services. We coordinate our installation sequence with the builder and other trades, and rely on the approved project information for matters that require specialist design, certification or authority approval. Clear hold points reduce avoidable rework in busy fitout programs.

sections.title: Durable finishes for high-touch spaces
sections.summary: A customer-facing counter, wall lining or display must suit its daily use, not only its opening-day appearance. We discuss edge details, impact-prone corners, cleaning methods, access panels and repairability when selecting materials and finishes. These decisions give owners a more practical result in areas exposed to bags, chairs, trolleys, cleaning and frequent contact.

sections.title: Occupied-site communication
sections.summary: Where work proceeds near staff or customers, orderly staging matters. We communicate with the responsible site contact about access, dust control expectations, protection, deliveries and day-to-day handovers. The exact controls depend on the building and scope, but the principle is constant: make work visible, coordinated and respectful of the people using the premises.

sections.title: Briefing a commercial refurbishment
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the premises, project stage, opening deadline and desired carpentry work. We assess the site, occupied areas and interfaces with other trades, then confirm the carpentry package and written quote. Existing drawings, tenancy requirements, programme and photos help if available; we agree any required approvals and final specifications before work begins.

services.title: Custom Kitchen & Bathroom Cabinetry
services.summary: Bespoke kitchen cabinets, islands, vanities and laundry units — designed and installed end to end, sized to your exact space.
services.lead: We build in our own workshop and control every dimension and joint, so cabinets install with zero rework and zero gaps.

sections.title: Full kitchen cabinetry
sections.summary: Upper and lower cabinets, island benches and hardware (Blum/Hettich) with stone or engineered-stone tops; solid-timber, 2-pac or moisture-resistant doors.

sections.title: Waterproof vanities
sections.summary: Vanities built on waterproof substrate with sealed backs, moisture-proof edging and stainless supports for wet areas.

sections.title: Laundry units
sections.summary: Stacking washer/dryer cabinets, storage and fold-out benches maximising space, with plumbing coordination.

sections.title: Measure & install
sections.summary: On-site measure → 3D design sign-off → workshop build → install, all by one team, no subcontracting.

sections.title: Begin with the way you cook and live
sections.summary: Good cabinetry is organised around real use: who cooks, what needs to be stored, where appliances sit, how doors open and how the room is cleaned. We discuss workflow, storage pain points, preferred materials and the visual relationship to adjoining rooms before locking in a layout. This makes the design more useful than a catalogue of cabinet sizes.

sections.title: Site measure and existing-condition checks
sections.summary: Walls are not always square, floors can vary and renovation services may not be where old drawings suggest. A detailed measure records dimensions, out-of-plumb conditions, service positions, access and adjoining finishes. This information is used to plan fillers, scribing, appliance clearances and installation tolerances before workshop production begins.

sections.title: Materials, hardware and moisture exposure
sections.summary: Door finish, cabinet board, edge treatment, benchtop interface and hardware all affect the way cabinetry performs. We explain options in terms of location and use, including areas exposed to steam, splashes or cleaning. Wet-area waterproofing, plumbing and electrical work remain coordinated with the appropriately qualified project trades and the approved design.

sections.title: Design approval before manufacture
sections.summary: Final drawings or agreed selections should clearly show layout, finishes, handles, appliance information, benchtop responsibility and any special details. Confirming these decisions before manufacture is an important quality step: it reduces late changes, allows lead times to be managed and ensures the client, builder and trades are working from the same intent.

sections.title: Installation and trade handover
sections.summary: Cabinets are installed in a planned sequence that considers floor finishes, wall readiness, stone templating, splashbacks and services. We protect completed work and coordinate practical handover points with other trades. Final adjustment includes checking door and drawer operation, visible alignment and the interfaces that can only be assessed once the room comes together.

sections.title: Useful information for a cabinetry consultation
sections.summary: Bring room dimensions or plans, photos, appliance models, inspiration images, storage requirements and an indication of the project stage. For bathrooms and laundries, include plumbing layout and wall finish information where available. The better the brief, the more accurately we can discuss a tailored Adelaide cabinetry solution and the decisions that affect cost and timing.

services.title: Architectural Joinery
services.summary: High-difficulty timber features for premium homes and commercial spaces — wall panelling, hidden doors, complex stair rails and feature ceilings.
services.lead: Architectural joinery is a core MEL ONE strength — turning a designer's complex vision into precisely built solid-timber product.

sections.title: Wall panelling
sections.summary: Material choice (Blackwood, American Oak) through to fixing — grooved modules, matched joins and open or closed grain finish.

sections.title: Hidden & pivot doors
sections.summary: Flush hidden doors, recessed handles and frameless detail, with door-in-wall and non-load-bearing installation options.

sections.title: Complex stair rails
sections.summary: Curved handrails, glass-and-timber balustrades with 3D set-out, custom pieces and on-site tuning.

sections.title: Feature ceilings & light coves
sections.summary: Large commercial timber ceilings, hidden cove lighting and acoustic panels with structural fixing plans.

sections.title: Turning a design concept into buildable detail
sections.summary: Architectural joinery often starts with a drawing, sketch or reference image that still needs practical decisions. We review proportions, substrate, fixing zones, junctions, access and the sequence of adjoining finishes. This translation from visual intent to buildable detail is where careful joinery planning prevents a premium feature from becoming difficult to install or maintain.

sections.title: Grain, colour and sample approval
sections.summary: Natural timber varies in grain, tone and figure; that variation is part of its character. We discuss the desired level of matching, board direction, veneer layout, stain or clear finish, and the effect of lighting before final selection. Samples and agreed reference points help clients understand what is being specified without promising that every piece of timber will be identical.

sections.title: Substrates, movement and fixing
sections.summary: Large panels, doors, rails and linings must be detailed for their substrate and environment. We consider access to fixing points, realistic tolerances, movement between materials and the future need to reach concealed services. Where a design requires engineered support, glazing or specialist hardware, those elements are coordinated through the relevant project professionals.

sections.title: Workshop preparation and site installation
sections.summary: Complex pieces benefit from a measured workflow: site verification, drawings or templates, workshop preparation, test fitting where practical, delivery protection and staged installation. This reduces surprise cutting on site and gives the team a controlled way to manage fine joins, shadow lines and continuous visual features across a room or commercial space.

sections.title: Detail review in the finished light
sections.summary: Joinery is experienced at close range and under the project's actual lighting. At completion we review alignment, gaps, edge treatment, door operation and the intended visual rhythm of the feature. The goal is not artificial perfection from every angle; it is a well-resolved piece that reads as deliberate, balanced and appropriate to its material.

sections.title: What to bring to an architectural joinery brief
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the feature and finish you want and the current project stage. We measure the site and confirm interfaces with hardware, lighting, stone or glazing, the manufacture and installation sequence and the written quote. Existing drawings, elevations, materials schedules, inspiration images and photos are optional for first contact. Final drawings, specifications and required approvals are agreed before manufacture.

services.title: Storage Solutions
services.summary: Bespoke wardrobes, display cases, study units and media walls — precise planning and durable hardware for high-use storage.
services.lead: Good storage design doubles a room. We design around real movement so everything has a place and still looks great.

sections.title: Walk-in wardrobes
sections.summary: Hanging, drawer, shoe and luggage zones with adjustable shelving that grows with you.

sections.title: Study units
sections.summary: Desk + bookcase + storage combos with hidden cable management, ergonomic height and monitor-arm provision.

sections.title: Media walls
sections.summary: TV wall mounts, speaker gear, media storage and decor in one wall, with cooling and concealed cabling.

sections.title: Display & wine cabinets
sections.summary: LED-lit glass-door displays and temperature-controlled wine cabinets for living, dining and commercial spaces.

sections.title: Map what needs to be stored
sections.summary: Storage works when it reflects actual belongings and routines. We ask about hanging lengths, folded items, files, toys, shoes, media equipment, cleaning tools and the objects clients want to display. Mapping these categories before design helps avoid beautiful cabinetry that has too little depth, too few drawers or inaccessible high shelves.

sections.title: Plan movement, reach and access
sections.summary: Doors, drawers and pull-outs need room to operate without blocking a bed, walkway, desk or adjacent cabinet. We consider everyday reach, clear floor area, opening direction and where power or ventilation is needed. The result is storage that supports the room rather than forcing people to work around it every time they use it.

sections.title: Internal fittings that earn their space
sections.summary: Adjustable shelves, hanging rails, drawers, pull-out baskets, integrated lighting and cable management each have a useful role when selected for a specific need. We discuss which fittings simplify daily use and which add cost without adding value. This keeps the design focused on durable, serviceable storage rather than features chosen only for a showroom effect.

sections.title: Walls, services and mounting conditions
sections.summary: Tall units, media walls and floating elements need to suit the wall construction, service routes and load they will carry. We check site conditions before finalising fixing and access details. Electrical, data, ventilation and other specialist services are coordinated with the relevant trades so the finished unit remains practical to use and maintain.

sections.title: Finishes that suit the room
sections.summary: A wardrobe, study or media unit should relate to light, flooring, adjoining joinery and the amount of wear it will receive. We can discuss timber, veneer, painted, laminate and glass elements in terms of appearance, cleaning and repairability. Samples help guide colour and texture decisions, particularly where new joinery meets an existing interior.

sections.title: Preparing for a custom-storage consultation
sections.summary: Photos, a rough room plan, ceiling height, wall dimensions and a list of what needs to be stored are an excellent starting point. Include appliances, screens or equipment that must fit, and note access restrictions in apartments or older homes. We measure the room and clearances on site, develop the storage layout around your needs and confirm the materials, installation scope and written quote.

services.title: Custom Doors, Windows & Furniture
services.summary: High-precision weatherproof timber doors and windows, plus one-off solid-timber tables and bars built with craft.
services.lead: From building windows to interior furniture, we use solid timber and precise joinery to make pieces that last.

sections.title: Solid weatherproof doors
sections.summary: AS 2047 compliant entry and side doors with triple-lock provision and sealed gaskets.

sections.title: Custom timber furniture
sections.summary: Dining, boardroom, bar, desk and bedside pieces to your space and habits, in local Blackwood, Oak or Jarrah.

sections.title: French & sliding doors
sections.summary: Timber French and sliding doors with custom tracks, acoustic seals and secure locking.

sections.title: Match the piece to its setting
sections.summary: A front door, heritage window, dining table and commercial bar have different performance, visual and maintenance needs. We begin with location, use, exposure, style and the relationship to surrounding finishes. This helps determine whether a solid-timber, engineered, glazed or mixed-material solution is appropriate before time is spent refining a profile or finish.

sections.title: Measure openings and interfaces carefully
sections.summary: Existing openings can conceal uneven walls, changes in floor level, old fixings and service conflicts. A site measure records the actual conditions, hardware requirements, weather exposure and installation access. For replacement work, we also discuss what adjoining trims, linings, render or paint may be affected so the scope is understood before manufacture or removal begins.

sections.title: Timber, glass, hardware and finish selection
sections.summary: Material and hardware choices influence security, weathering, feel and long-term maintenance. We explain the practical role of species, profile, glazing interface, hinges, tracks, locks, seals and coating systems. Where performance or regulatory requirements apply, the product selection and project documentation need to be coordinated with the appropriate designer, supplier or certifier.

sections.title: Furniture built for daily use
sections.summary: For a table, desk, bench or bar, dimensions should follow the people and tasks it will serve. We discuss seating, leg clearance, cable needs, edge profiles, movement of solid timber and the type of wear the surface will receive. These details create furniture that is comfortable and repairable, not simply a striking object on delivery day.

sections.title: Workshop finish and installation care
sections.summary: Fine timber work benefits from controlled preparation, protection in transport and careful site handling. We plan the order of finishing, hardware fitting, delivery and installation so exposed faces and edges are not unnecessarily damaged. Once fitted, we check alignment, operation and visible junctions, then discuss any care requirements relevant to the selected finish.

sections.title: A useful custom-piece enquiry
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the intended use, timber or finish preferences and target timing. Existing photos, approximate dimensions, sketches, drawings and inspiration images are optional for the first enquiry; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. For external doors and windows, describe the opening and orientation; for furniture, describe who will use it. We measure on site and confirm the design, materials and quote before manufacture.

services.title: Restoration & Maintenance
services.summary: Repair of termite and moisture timber damage to frames, floors and doors — assessment, safe repair and preventative treatment.
services.lead: Older Adelaide homes carry real termite risk. We offer assessment-to-repair in one team and advise on prevention.

sections.title: Termite damage repair
sections.summary: With a licensed pest controller, we assess extent and impact, replace damaged frames, floor joists and door jambs, and install termite barriers.

sections.title: Moisture rot repair
sections.summary: Repair of water-damaged timber with waterproofing, ventilation improvement, member replacement and damp-proof coating.

sections.title: Structural assessment
sections.summary: Pre-repair structural safety check, with engineer's report where needed to meet the Building Code.

sections.title: Diagnose the cause before repairing the symptom
sections.summary: Rot, movement, staining, jammed doors and soft timber can point to more than one cause. We start by observing the affected area, moisture paths, ventilation, nearby services and the extent that can be seen safely. Repairing only the visible face without addressing the underlying water, pest or movement issue can create a short-lived result and unnecessary repeat cost.

sections.title: Make the damaged area safe and accessible
sections.summary: MEL ONE checks the damaged timber and arranges a safe assessment of the affected area. We discuss any temporary protection, support or access work needed, identify the repair scope and confirm the quote. Where pest, electrical, plumbing, engineering or hazardous-material work is required, we confirm the qualified service arrangements before permanent work begins.

sections.title: Repair, splice or replace
sections.summary: Not every damaged timber member needs complete replacement, and not every local patch is suitable. We discuss what is sound, what needs to be removed, how the repaired area will connect to existing work and what finishing repairs follow. The chosen method should suit the member's role, access and condition, with structural decisions referred to the appropriate project professional where necessary.

sections.title: Coordinate moisture and pest prevention
sections.summary: Carpentry repair is often one part of a broader remedy. Drainage, flashing, plumbing leaks, ventilation, coatings and pest management may all affect the long-term outcome. We identify the interfaces that need attention and coordinate our scope with the owner, builder or specialist trades so a repaired timber element is not returned to the same damaging conditions.

sections.title: Document condition and agreed scope
sections.summary: We inspect the affected timber and joints on site and explain the repair scope before work starts. If opening a concealed area is needed, we discuss and agree that work with you first. Photos and condition notes support clear decisions and handover records.

sections.title: What to send for a repair assessment
sections.summary: Photos from near and far, the address, age or type of building, when the issue was first noticed, and any reports from pest, plumbing or building professionals are helpful. Mention access limitations and whether the area is occupied. MEL ONE uses this information to prepare the site assessment. We inspect the timber, investigate moisture or movement concerns and confirm the restoration scope and written quote, including any qualified investigation required.

services.title: Heritage Carpentry
services.summary: Traditional timber repair for South Australian heritage-listed buildings — mortise-and-tenon joinery and period window restoration.
services.lead: Heritage repair needs expertise and respect for history. We know the SA Heritage Act and combine traditional craft with modern technique to protect heritage value.

sections.title: Mortise & tenon repair
sections.summary: Dovetail, through, and groove joints inspected, repaired and remade with period-matched timber and hand tools.

sections.title: Carved trim restoration
sections.summary: Heritage cornices, eave brackets and carved panels restored by joiners with traditional experience.

sections.title: Period window restoration
sections.summary: Box and picket sash windows returned to original with replicated hardware, period glass and paint system.

sections.title: Record original fabric before intervention
sections.summary: Heritage timber carries information in its profiles, joints, glass, hardware and layers of finish. We begin by documenting the visible condition and identifying elements that can be retained, repaired or carefully replicated. This gives owners and project teams a clearer basis for deciding how to preserve the character of a place while addressing practical performance issues.

sections.title: Understand approvals and project responsibilities
sections.summary: Heritage work can involve owner, architect, heritage adviser, builder and approval authority responsibilities that vary by property and scope. We do not assume a single rule applies to every Adelaide building. Instead, we work from the approved project information and coordinate the carpentry detail with the people responsible for heritage advice, design and approvals where these are required.

sections.title: Repair first, replace only where justified
sections.summary: Sound original material often has value beyond its appearance. We assess whether local repairs, splices, consolidation, new sections or full replication are appropriate to the observed condition and intended performance. The aim is a clear, honest repair strategy—not a cosmetic replacement that loses defining proportions or evidence of the building's original construction.

sections.title: Match profiles, species and detailing
sections.summary: When new timber is needed, profiles, grain direction, joinery detail and interfaces are considered alongside the existing work. Exact historic matching may not always be possible or appropriate, so decisions are discussed in the context of the approved design and available materials. Samples or templates can help resolve visible details before work proceeds across a larger elevation or repeated feature.

sections.title: Windows, doors and ongoing care
sections.summary: Traditional openings depend on many small elements working together: sashes, cords, weights, stops, weathering details, glazing and paint systems. We review operation and visible condition as part of the carpentry scope, while specialist glazing, coatings or performance requirements are coordinated with the relevant trades. Ongoing inspection helps identify coating or water-entry issues before more substantial damage develops.

sections.title: Arrange a heritage carpentry assessment
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the address, timber elements and concerns you have noticed. Existing heritage advice, approvals, drawings, history and safe photos help if available, but are optional for first contact. We assess the timber on site, identify what can be retained or repaired and confirm the restoration plan and quote, including qualified heritage input and approval requirements.

services.title: Decking Restoration & Timber Flooring
services.summary: Deck sanding, oiling and staining plus timber floor laying and refinishing — solid and engineered, full service.
services.lead: Floors and decks live or die by maintenance frequency and method. We handle new laying and regular care so your timber stays new.

sections.title: Timber floor laying
sections.summary: Solid and engineered timber with damp-proof underlay, expansion gaps and accurate levelling.

sections.title: Deck sanding & oiling
sections.summary: High-pressure sanding to remove old coating and mould, fine graded paper, then penetrating oil or stain to restore natural colour.

sections.title: Floor refinishing
sections.summary: Worn floors sanded and refinished to original gloss and feel, with edge detailing.

sections.title: Assess the timber beneath the finish
sections.summary: Before recommending sanding, coating or replacement, we look at the condition that can be seen: board movement, staining, worn coating, gaps, previous repairs, moisture clues and access to edges. A timber surface may need cosmetic work, local repair or a broader subfloor investigation. Understanding the difference helps owners choose an appropriate scope rather than applying a finish over an unresolved problem.

sections.title: Choose an outcome, not just a colour
sections.summary: The desired result might be a refreshed natural look, a more even tone, reduced slipperiness, a darker stain or a finish that is easier to maintain. We discuss how timber species, existing coatings, sunlight and prior repairs affect those choices. Samples and test areas can be useful when a client wants to see how a proposed product reads in the actual room or outdoor setting.

sections.title: Prepare the space and manage interfaces
sections.summary: Floor and deck work is affected by furniture, access, weather, dust control, adjacent finishes and curing time. We plan practical preparation with the client or builder so the work area can be accessed safely and completed surfaces are protected. External work is scheduled with realistic attention to weather and drying conditions rather than promises that ignore the site environment.

sections.title: Repair boards, edges and transitions
sections.summary: A quality refresh often includes more than the open field of boards. Edges, thresholds, loose fixings, local damage, stair nosings and junctions to tile or carpet may need attention to make the completed surface feel resolved. We discuss these details upfront because they affect both appearance and the practical sequence of the work.

sections.title: Care after sanding, oiling or coating
sections.summary: Newly treated timber benefits from the right early care and a realistic maintenance routine. We explain what to avoid while finishes settle, how to clean without unnecessary abrasion and what signs suggest it is time to review a high-wear or high-exposure area. The useful interval depends on the timber, finish, traffic, sun and moisture—not a generic calendar promise.

sections.title: Information for a flooring or deck review
sections.summary: Describe the flooring or deck condition and your preferred finish. Existing daylight photos, approximate area, material or coating history are optional; do not enter an unsafe underside to photograph it. We inspect the timber, fixings, moisture exposure and drainage on site and confirm maintenance, repair or replacement work and the quote.

services.title: Door & Window Repairs
services.summary: Practical repairs for timber doors, window frames, sashes and trim — assess sticking, weathering and local damage before deciding the right next step.
services.lead: MEL ONE repairs timber doors and windows in Adelaide. We inspect the opening, timber, hardware and adjoining trim on site, identify the adjustment or repair needed and confirm the work plan and written quote.

sections.title: What door and window repair can cover
sections.summary: A repair can involve a timber door leaf, frame, jamb, sash, sill, architrave or local trim. The useful starting point is the part that is actually affected: a door may stick because of movement, a damaged edge, hardware adjustment or a changed floor level, while a window problem may relate to a sash, frame, weather-exposed timber or surrounding finish. We discuss the observed condition before assuming a single cause.

sections.title: Common signs worth recording
sections.summary: Owners may notice rubbing doors, misaligned latches, loose trim, peeling paint, soft timber, difficult windows or draughts. Tell MEL ONE what has changed, including whether it follows rain or seasonal movement. Safely taken whole-opening and detail photos are optional. We check the timber, hardware and adjoining surfaces on site and confirm local repair, adjustment or any wider condition assessment required.

sections.title: Condition, water and surrounding materials
sections.summary: Timber deterioration can be local, but it is important to understand the conditions around it. Water paths, failed coatings, end grain, flashing, glazing, seals and junctions to masonry or cladding can all influence a repair decision. Replacing a visibly damaged piece without considering why it deteriorated may leave the same exposure unresolved. We keep the carpentry scope clear and identify adjoining glazing, coating or building-envelope work that may need coordination.

sections.title: Repair, local replacement or a new element
sections.summary: The right approach depends on how much sound material remains, the visible profile, daily use and the purpose of the opening. Some problems can be resolved with careful adjustment or a local timber repair; others need a replacement component or a wider discussion about the frame and adjoining finish. For older Adelaide homes, maintaining proportions and interfaces can matter as much as restoring operation. We explain the practical options rather than presenting cosmetic replacement as the only answer.

sections.title: Planning access and hardware
sections.summary: Doors and windows are used every day, so access and timing affect the work. Tell us which rooms are involved, whether the opening must remain secure or weather-protected, the type of hardware present and whether the work is part of painting, glazing or a renovation. Photos of hinges, latches, locks and problem areas help establish the likely carpentry tasks. Specialist hardware, glazing or security requirements should be identified early so the correct trade interfaces can be planned.

sections.title: Working with heritage and existing joinery
sections.summary: MEL ONE inspects older timber openings, records the profiles and joints, and identifies sound material to retain and damaged sections to repair or replicate. We check the repair requirements and discuss the project documents, access and approved scope with you before work begins. Contact our Adelaide team to arrange an assessment and quote.

sections.title: Information for a useful repair enquiry
sections.summary: Describe when the door or window problem occurs, your Adelaide suburb and the number of openings. Existing daylight photos and approximate sizes are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. Tell us about planned painting, glazing or flooring. We inspect the openings on site and confirm the repair sequence, any related trim or qualified glazing arrangements and the written quote.

services.title: Skirting Board Installation & Repairs
services.summary: New, replacement and repaired skirting boards for Adelaide interiors — planned around wall condition, flooring transitions, timber profiles and paint-ready finishing.
services.lead: MEL ONE installs and repairs skirting boards for Adelaide homes, renovations and fit-outs. We consider the room, existing trim, finished floor height and adjacent door details so the completed line looks intentional and works with the rest of the interior.

sections.title: New skirting, replacement and local repair
sections.summary: Skirting work can range from replacing a damaged length to fitting a consistent profile through a renovated room or full home. The right scope depends on what is already in place, whether the wall line is changing and how the skirting meets door jambs, stairs, cabinetry and flooring. We discuss whether matching, selective repair or a new continuous treatment best suits the visible condition and the wider finishing work.

sections.title: Profiles, material and the existing room
sections.summary: A skirting profile changes the character of a room and the way trim joins read at corners and openings. Existing height, shape, material, paint build-up and wall condition all affect a matching decision. Where a profile is being selected for a new space, it should be considered alongside architraves, doors, cabinetry and floor finishes rather than in isolation. Samples, photos and a clear reference point help avoid a result that looks unrelated to adjoining rooms.

sections.title: Floor levels and practical transitions
sections.summary: Skirtings sit at the meeting point of wall and floor, so final floor thickness, carpet, timber, tile and threshold details matter. A room may have uneven floors, newly installed flooring or an existing gap from an earlier finish. We review those transitions before fixing the trim, particularly where a new floor will follow after carpentry. This lets the scope allow for neat junctions without treating a changing floor level as an afterthought.

sections.title: Corners, returns and irregular walls
sections.summary: Older walls, external corners, bay windows, stair strings and built-ins need careful measuring. MEL ONE checks the room and plans cutting, returns and joins for a consistent skirting finish. We explain any wall or floor adjustments in the agreed scope and quote.

sections.title: Repairing damaged or missing sections
sections.summary: Water, moving furniture, pets, previous alterations and removed cabinetry can leave skirting with chips, breaks, stains or missing lengths. A local repair may be appropriate where the surrounding profile and material are sound. When damage is widespread, a longer replacement section may create a more consistent result. We assess what can be seen and make clear where concealed wall, floor or moisture conditions could affect the final extent of work.

sections.title: Coordination with paint, doors and cabinetry
sections.summary: The most successful interior finish comes from sequencing. Painting, flooring, door hanging, joinery installation and skirting work can affect one another, especially where caulking, filling, coating and touch-up responsibilities differ. Let us know what stage the room is at and which trades are still to follow. We can then discuss when trim should be measured and installed, and how it will connect to new door jambs, wardrobes or kitchen cabinetry.

sections.title: Details that help us prepare the site measure
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE whether you need skirting repair, profile matching or new installation, and which rooms are involved. Photos, approximate dimensions and a sketch are optional for first contact; existing floor-finish and planned-door details help us prepare. We measure the junctions on site, check wet areas, curves and built-ins and confirm the profile, work scope and written quote.

services.title: Door Jambs & Interior Trim
services.summary: Door jamb, architrave and interior trim carpentry for Adelaide homes — focused on clean reveals, practical door operation and coordinated second-fix details.
services.lead: MEL ONE provides Adelaide door-jamb and interior-trim carpentry for renovations, repairs and finishing stages. We plan the frame, architraves, reveals and adjacent flooring or cabinetry details together, so a door opening is practical to use and visually resolved.

sections.title: What interior trim work includes
sections.summary: Interior trim may include a new or repaired door jamb, architraves, reveals, stop details, casing, local lining repairs and junctions to skirtings. It is often part of second-fix carpentry, but it can also be a focused repair after a door change, wall alteration or water-damage rectification. We define the actual opening and adjoining finishes before deciding whether the work needs a local adjustment, replacement component or a coordinated finishing package.

sections.title: Jambs, reveals and door operation
sections.summary: A door frame needs to work with the wall thickness, finished floor, leaf, hardware and swing. Small differences in plumb, floor level, lining thickness or hinge position can affect the final clearances. We review these practical relationships before final fixing and trim installation. Where a door is sticking, binding or no longer closing cleanly, photographs and notes about the change over time help distinguish an adjustment question from a wider jamb, leaf or surrounding-building issue.

sections.title: Architraves and visible proportions
sections.summary: Architraves create the transition from opening to wall, so profile, width, corner treatment and the relationship to skirting are immediately visible. In a renovation, an existing profile may need to be matched or a new trim language chosen for the room. We use the observed room details, reference photos and finishes schedule to guide that decision. The aim is not to overcomplicate a simple opening, but to prevent new trim from looking disconnected from adjacent doors and rooms.

sections.title: Existing walls and changed openings
sections.summary: Renovated homes may have patched linings, uneven wall thickness, former openings, new bulkheads or changed floor levels around a door. These conditions can influence the jamb depth, reveal detail and the amount of trim work needed to create a clean transition. We assess what is visible and identify where opening-up or another trade’s work may be needed before a final finish is possible. Clear scope boundaries avoid a trim allowance masking unresolved wall or structural changes.

sections.title: Hardware and specialist requirements
sections.summary: Hinges, latches, locks, seals and handles need to be selected and coordinated with the door and frame. Tell us whether hardware is supplied, whether the opening has acoustic, security, fire or accessibility requirements in approved project documents, and whether another trade is managing those elements. We do not assume specialist performance requirements from appearance alone; identifying them early helps the relevant project team plan the right product, installation sequence and checks.

sections.title: Second-fix sequencing
sections.summary: Door jamb and trim work normally sits between plastering, flooring, painting, cabinetry and door-hanging tasks. Starting before wall linings or floors are ready can create repeated work or inconsistent junctions. We discuss room readiness, material delivery, access and the finish responsibilities before installation. This is especially useful where multiple rooms are being renovated in stages and the owner needs a sensible order for doors, skirtings, built-ins and paint preparation.

sections.title: Preparing an Adelaide trim enquiry
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the proposed door type, hardware, current build stage and trim that needs matching. Existing photos of the opening or trim and approximate measurements are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. We measure the opening, wall thickness and floor-finish transitions on site, check nearby skirtings and cabinetry, and confirm the door-jamb, architrave and second-fix work in the quote.

services.title: Timber Fencing Repairs & Replacement
services.summary: Timber fence repairs and replacement for Adelaide properties — inspect palings, rails, posts and access conditions before choosing a practical scope.
services.lead: MEL ONE helps Adelaide owners plan timber fencing repairs and replacement work. We consider the fence condition, access, adjacent outdoor structures and the difference between a local repair and a longer replacement section before setting out the next step.

sections.title: Understanding the affected part of a fence
sections.summary: A timber fence is made up of palings or boards, rails, posts, caps, gates and connections to the ground or other structures. Visible damage may be limited to one panel, or it may indicate movement, decay, impact damage or a wider issue at posts and rails. We begin with the observed area and its connections, rather than assuming that a leaning fence can be resolved by replacing the most visible paling alone.

sections.title: Repair versus replacement
sections.summary: MEL ONE inspects the fence boards, rails, posts and connections on site. We identify whether a local repair or a larger replacement suits the condition, access and matching requirements, then confirm the timber work and quote with you.

sections.title: Posts, rails and ground conditions
sections.summary: Posts and rails carry the fence, so their condition influences the scope even when the visible problem is at the face. Soil, drainage, garden beds, retaining edges and previous repairs can affect access and the way a replacement is approached. Tell us if the fence is near a deck, paving, pool area, service line or mature planting. These details help identify practical constraints and avoid treating a boundary fence as an isolated decorative panel.

sections.title: Matching an existing timber fence
sections.summary: When only part of a fence is being repaired, height, board style, rail arrangement and finish can influence how well new work sits beside old. Weathered timber may not match a new section immediately, and staining or painting is often a separate finishing decision. Photos taken from both sides of the fence help establish the visible layout. We discuss reasonable matching expectations and any profile or material decisions before work begins.

sections.title: Boundary access and project responsibilities
sections.summary: Fence work can involve neighbours, side access, pets, landscaping and shared boundaries. MEL ONE discusses the property agreements, approvals and boundary information with the authorised owner or site contact before scheduling work. We confirm safe access, the timber repair scope and the sequence in your quote.

sections.title: Fences beside decks and outdoor living areas
sections.summary: A fence can affect privacy, circulation, shade, gate placement and the way a deck or pergola meets the boundary. If the work connects to an outdoor-living upgrade, share the broader plan so posts, screens and edges are considered together. Coordinating related timber work early can reduce awkward junctions and repeated disturbance to finished landscaping. The scope should still distinguish fence work from decking, drainage, electrical and other trade packages.

sections.title: Details for a useful fencing enquiry
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE which fence sections need attention, what has moved or broken and any nearby gates, structures, slopes or garden beds. Safely taken photos and approximate lengths or heights are optional. We check posts, rails, panels, access and ground conditions on site, explain repair or replacement options and confirm the agreed scope and written quote.

services.title: Timber Gate Installation & Repairs
services.summary: Timber pedestrian and access-gate installation and repair for Adelaide properties — planned around alignment, hinges, latches, privacy and fence integration.
services.lead: MEL ONE provides Adelaide timber gate installation and repair planning for pedestrian gates, side access and garden entries. We consider the opening, gate weight, hardware, fence condition and everyday use so the scope addresses operation as well as appearance.

sections.title: A gate is more than its timber face
sections.summary: A working timber gate depends on the leaf, frame, posts, hinges, latch, clearance and the fence or structure it joins. A gate that drags or will not latch may have a local hardware issue, but it can also reflect movement in posts, a changed ground level, swelling timber or a mismatched leaf and opening. We assess the practical relationship between these elements before deciding whether adjustment, repair or a new gate is appropriate.

sections.title: New gates for access and privacy
sections.summary: A new side gate, pedestrian gate or garden entry should suit how the area is used. Opening direction, clear width, rubbish-bin or garden access, privacy, sight lines and the relationship to a deck or path all affect the layout. Tell MEL ONE the access and style you want; existing photos and approximate measurements are optional via handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com. We measure the opening, check the existing fence and confirm the gate design, hardware and quote.

sections.title: Gate alignment and daily movement
sections.summary: Hinges, latch position, clearance to paving and the condition of the supporting post all influence gate operation. Timber can move with weather and exposure, while paths or landscaping may change over time. We review how the gate currently behaves, including any rubbing, sagging, loose hardware or difficulty engaging the latch. This gives a better basis for repair than simply replacing a hinge without considering the rest of the opening.

sections.title: Hardware and security coordination
sections.summary: A gate’s hardware should match the intended use, whether that is a simple garden latch, a more secure side entry or integration with another access arrangement. Tell us what hardware is currently present, whether it is being supplied, and whether locks, automation, intercoms or electrical items are involved. Those specialist elements may require coordination with the appropriate trade. We keep the carpentry work clearly scoped around the timber gate, supports and practical installation details.

sections.title: Repairing an existing timber gate
sections.summary: Existing gates can suffer from weathering, damaged boards, loose rails, worn hinges, movement at posts or changes in the adjoining fence. A repair may involve local timber work, hardware adjustment or a more complete rebuild depending on the soundness of the remaining components. Photos of the front and back, the hinges, latch and post bases are useful. Where decay or movement is concealed, the scope should allow for a condition review once the affected area is accessible.

sections.title: Integrating gates with fencing and outdoor work
sections.summary: A new gate often meets a fence, screen, deck, retaining edge or paved path. Considering those interfaces early helps maintain clear access and avoids a gate swing conflicting with furniture, steps or planting. If fencing and outdoor-living work are planned together, explain the broader outcome so related elements can be sequenced sensibly. The quotation can then distinguish the gate from adjoining carpentry, landscaping, electrical or boundary responsibilities.

sections.title: What to include in a gate enquiry
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE how the gate will be used, the opening direction and any existing hardware or nearby fence and path issues. Photos and approximate dimensions are optional for first contact. Mention pets, children, shared access and security needs. We measure the opening and check hinges, posts, latch and clearances on site, then confirm repair or installation requirements and the written quote.

services.title: Renovation Carpentry
services.summary: Adelaide renovation carpentry for existing homes — coordinate altered openings, timber repairs, trim, joinery interfaces and staged interior work.
services.lead: MEL ONE provides Adelaide renovation carpentry for homes where existing conditions, new finishes and multiple trades need to meet cleanly. We help define the timber scope around openings, trim, repairs, cabinetry and the sequence of work before the project reaches its finishing stage.

sections.title: Renovation carpentry starts with the existing home
sections.summary: An existing home brings conditions that drawings may not show: uneven walls, changed floor levels, previous alterations, concealed services, old trim and materials that need careful matching. We begin by understanding the rooms, the proposed changes and what can be observed before work starts. This creates a practical carpentry scope for altered openings, repairs and finishes without assuming that an older room will behave like a new empty shell.

sections.title: Defining the timber scope across a renovation
sections.summary: Renovation carpentry can include framing changes directed by approved documentation, door openings, jambs, skirtings, architraves, local timber repairs, joinery interfaces and finishing details. The best scope is clear about which elements belong to MEL ONE and which are managed by the builder, designer, plumber, electrician, plasterer, painter or cabinetmaker. Clear boundaries protect the project program and help the owner understand what needs to happen before each room can be finished.

sections.title: Openings, trims and finished floor levels
sections.summary: Doorways, windows, cabinetry and floor transitions are where a renovation becomes visibly precise or visibly unresolved. The jamb depth, trim profile, reveal, skirting height and floor finish need to be considered together. We discuss those details before final fixing, particularly when new timber flooring, tile, carpet or cabinetry will change existing levels. This reduces the need for improvised packing, uneven lines or repeated trimming after other work is complete.

sections.title: Local timber repair within broader work
sections.summary: Removing an old cabinet, changing a wall or opening a lining can reveal damaged trim, missing skirting, rough framing or water-affected timber. MEL ONE checks the accessible area on site, defines the initial carpentry scope and discusses any opening-up needed. We agree changes to the repair plan, price and timing with you before additional work proceeds.

sections.title: Coordinating cabinetry and other trades
sections.summary: Kitchen, bathroom, storage and architectural joinery work depends on finished walls, floors, services and openings being ready at the right time. Carpentry may need to create backing, trim an opening, prepare a wall junction or complete skirtings after built-ins are fitted. Share the current drawings, finishes and trade program where available. Coordinating these interfaces early helps avoid cabinetry being measured before adjacent construction is settled or completed trim being damaged by later installation.

sections.title: Staging work around everyday living
sections.summary: Many Adelaide renovations take place while the property remains occupied. Access, dust, temporary security, room-by-room sequencing, furniture protection and the availability of bathrooms or kitchens can all affect how carpentry is scheduled. Let us know which rooms must stay usable and the preferred work windows. A realistic staged plan helps the owner, builder and trades decide what can be completed together and what should wait until adjoining work is ready.

sections.title: Preparing a renovation carpentry brief
sections.summary: Useful information includes current plans or sketches, photos of each affected room, the address, approximate project timing, intended finishes and a list of the outcomes you want. Mark altered openings, new doors, storage, kitchen or bathroom work, damaged timber and areas needing new trim. This lets MEL ONE discuss an Adelaide renovation carpentry scope that links the practical timber tasks to the wider project rather than treating each small junction as an isolated repair.

services.title: Adelaide Deck Replacement: When Boards, Joists or Fixings Need Attention
services.summary: A practical Adelaide deck replacement guide: how to distinguish surface wear from structural issues, what to inspect before requesting a quote, and how to scope a safer long-term repair.
services.lead: A deck can look tired for cosmetic reasons, or it can be signalling a deeper problem. Separating the two before work is priced helps homeowners make a sound decision.

sections.title: Start with the part that has actually failed
sections.summary: Deck boards commonly weather first: raised grain, splinters, loose fasteners and localised rot can make the surface uncomfortable without proving that the frame needs replacement. A closer inspection should also include joists, bearers, posts, connection points and the timber where it meets the house. Soft timber, persistent movement, visible decay around fasteners or a deck that no longer drains freely are reasons to investigate the structure rather than simply re-oil the surface.

sections.title: How Adelaide exposure affects maintenance priorities
sections.summary: Sun, rain and coastal air do not affect every Adelaide deck in the same way. An exposed western deck may need a different finishing cycle from a sheltered courtyard, while salt-laden air can accelerate corrosion where the wrong fixings have been used. The useful starting point is not a generic lifespan claim: note the deck orientation, shade, moisture paths, proximity to the coast and whether leaf litter or planter boxes keep sections damp.

sections.title: Prepare a quote-ready scope
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the deck location, preferred material, access constraints and whether you want the existing frame checked for reuse. Existing wide photos, close-ups and plans are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. We inspect the frame, measure the deck and check stairs, balustrades, seating and posts. The quote separates demolition, structural repairs, boards, stairs, handrails, finishing and waste removal, with any site-dependent items explained.

sections.title: Choose the next step based on evidence
sections.summary: MEL ONE inspects the deck boards, frame, post bases and connections on site to identify the repair required. We explain whether selective board replacement or a wider repair suits the condition, discuss approvals and engineering requirements, and confirm the work scope and quote before structural changes begin.

sections.title: Read the deck from the ground up
sections.summary: A useful inspection follows the load path rather than stopping at the top boards. Look at the ground contact points, footings, posts, bearers, joists, blocking, fixings and the way water leaves the area. This order helps separate a surface-maintenance issue from a question that needs a more detailed structural assessment.

sections.title: Material choices after removal
sections.summary: Once the existing construction is understood, the replacement decision can be specific: retain sound framing, replace damaged members, choose a board profile, resolve edge details and confirm how stairs or balustrades meet the new work. Comparing options against exposure, maintenance preference and intended use is more useful than selecting timber only by colour.

sections.title: Avoid the common repair shortcuts
sections.summary: Covering decayed timber, tightening a loose board without finding the cause, or applying a fresh coating to a damp surface may improve appearance briefly without solving the condition below. A transparent scope identifies unknown areas, access limitations and the sequence for opening or repairing them, so the client can make an informed decision about risk and budget.

sections.title: Coordinate stairs, balustrades and adjacent work
sections.summary: Deck replacement often touches more than boards. Stairs, privacy screens, roof posts, planters, lighting, pools and external doors can affect the workable sequence. Mapping these interfaces before demolition helps preserve access and avoids a new deck being held up by an overlooked connection, service or finish that belongs to another part of the project.

sections.title: Questions to ask at handover
sections.summary: Ask which members were retained or replaced, what finish has been applied, how water is intended to drain, what areas need periodic review and how to report a concern. Keeping photographs of the work before boards are closed over can also be useful for future maintenance. Clear handover information is part of a durable deck, not an optional extra.

services.title: Adelaide Custom Wardrobe Planning: How to Measure, Specify and Avoid Storage Dead Space
services.summary: Plan a custom wardrobe for an Adelaide home with a practical checklist for measurements, internal storage, doors, materials and installation access before final design and pricing.
services.lead: MEL ONE turns your Adelaide custom wardrobe brief into a measured layout, an agreed materials and hardware specification, and a clear installation quote. Start with how you use the space, then confirm the site details before manufacture.

sections.title: Measure the room, then measure the obstructions
sections.summary: Overall width, height and depth are only the first layer. Note skirtings, cornices, power points, windows, light switches, return walls and door swings, plus any variation in floor or wall level. In older Adelaide homes, walls and ceilings are not always square; an on-site measure before manufacture is the point at which the cabinet dimensions, filler panels and scribe details can be finalised.

sections.title: Turn daily habits into internal zones
sections.summary: List what the wardrobe must hold before selecting finishes. Long-hang clothing, folded garments, shoes, linen, bags, drawers and seasonal storage each need different clearances. A useful layout normally mixes adjustable shelves with dedicated hanging zones and avoids deep, unlit shelves that become dead space. Consider who uses each side of the wardrobe and whether future changes—such as a child growing or a room changing function—are likely.

sections.title: Select doors and materials for the room, not the showroom
sections.summary: Hinged doors need clear swing space; sliding doors preserve circulation but limit access to part of the interior at once. Mirrored, painted and timber-look finishes each change light, maintenance and the visual weight of the room. For wardrobes near bathrooms, laundries or external walls, discuss moisture exposure and ventilation so the substrate, edging and installation detail suit the location.

sections.title: Plan the installation as carefully as the cabinet
sections.summary: Confirm access from the street to the room, stair turns, parking, flooring protection and the timing of painting, electrical work and new carpet. A clear installation sequence reduces the risk that joinery is measured before adjoining finishes are ready. To request a quote, tell MEL ONE what the wardrobe needs to store and the finishes you prefer. Existing room photos, a rough sketch and approximate measurements are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. MEL ONE confirms the room and access measurements on site.

sections.title: Set realistic depths and clearances
sections.summary: The internal depth, drawer projection, hanging clearance and shelf spacing must work with the garments and room, not just fit a nominal cabinet size. A wardrobe can lose useful capacity when a door, bed or window restricts access. Discussing these constraints early allows the layout to favour the items used daily and reserve higher or deeper areas for occasional storage.

sections.title: Use light, power and ventilation deliberately
sections.summary: Integrated lighting, power points and ventilation can make a wardrobe easier to use, but they need to be planned before the unit is built. Identify what requires electrical coordination, where cables or drivers can be accessed and whether exterior walls or adjoining wet areas create condensation concerns. These interfaces are resolved with the appropriate trades rather than retrofitted blindly.

sections.title: Understand visible finish and tolerance
sections.summary: Filler panels, scribes and small shadow lines are often the practical way for cabinetry to meet existing walls that are not straight. They should be treated as considered details, not defects. Reviewing samples, handle positions and the intended reveal between doors gives everyone a shared expectation before a custom wardrobe is manufactured and installed.

sections.title: Plan for changing needs
sections.summary: A well-planned wardrobe can adapt when a child's room changes, a guest room becomes a study or a household's storage mix evolves. Adjustable shelves, removable rails and sensible drawer sizing can offer flexibility without making the interior feel generic. The right choices depend on the client’s likely use, rather than adding every accessory available.

sections.title: Review before final sign-off
sections.summary: At completion, check door movement, drawer operation, alignment, visible edges, hardware and the way the unit meets the floor, wall and ceiling. Keep care information for the selected surface and note any access points for lighting or services. A brief practical review lets small adjustments be identified while the installation team and materials are still available.

sections.title: From your first brief to an agreed wardrobe scope
sections.summary: Start with a storage list and the door or finish options you want. Existing room photos and approximate dimensions are optional; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. MEL ONE then carries out the site measure, checks walls, floors and access, and confirms the proposed internal layout. Review door movement, drawer projection, hardware clearances, filler details and any lighting interfaces together. Approve the drawings and specification before the final quoted scope proceeds to manufacture and installation.

sections.title: What your wardrobe quote should include
sections.summary: The quote should describe the wardrobe location, layout and quantities: hanging zones, shelves, drawers and any selected accessories. Identify the cabinet substrate, edging, visible finishes, door material, handles and hardware. Confirm whether removal of an existing unit, transport, floor and room protection, waste removal, installation, wall or trim making-good, and lighting interfaces are included. Record exclusions and responsibilities clearly so the total scope is easy to compare.

sections.title: Keep a budget estimate separate from the confirmed quote
sections.summary: An early budget estimate uses the information and selections available at that stage. A confirmed quote follows the site measure and agreed layout, materials, hardware and installation conditions. Where something still needs checking, record the assumption and how it will be resolved. Ask MEL ONE to explain the pricing basis and included costs rather than treating a photo-based estimate as an approved manufacturing specification.

sections.title: Approve changes before manufacture or installation
sections.summary: Adding drawers, changing hinged doors to sliding doors or selecting a different door material can change hardware, internal access, fabrication and installation work. MEL ONE records the revised layout or specification and explains the effect on price and scheduling in a written variation. Approve that change before the affected work proceeds; keep the approved version alongside the original quote.

sections.title: Complete a practical wardrobe handover
sections.summary: At handover, compare the installed layout and visible finish with the approved scope. Operate the doors and drawers, check handles, alignment, shelving and agreed lighting access, and record any adjustments or outstanding work. Keep the surface-care information and final specification with the completion record. This gives the household a useful reference for routine care and future changes.

faqs.question: Can I get a final wardrobe price from room photos?
faqs.answer: Photos and approximate measurements help MEL ONE discuss an initial budget. The confirmed quote follows the site measure, agreed design and specification, and installation arrangements.
