faqs.question: What happens if I add drawers or change the doors?
faqs.answer: We revise the layout, materials and hardware requirements, explain the effect on price and scheduling, and obtain approval for a written variation before the affected work proceeds.

faqs.question: Does the wardrobe quote include removal and making-good?
faqs.answer: Check the written scope. Removal, transport, protection, waste, installation and making-good should each be listed as included, excluded or separately agreed.

faqs.question: What should I keep after installation?
faqs.answer: Keep the approved design and specification, quote and variations, care information, and handover record showing completed work and any agreed follow-up.

services.title: Adelaide Heritage Timber Repairs: A Practical Scope for Doors, Windows and External Joinery
services.summary: A practical guide to scoping heritage timber repairs in Adelaide, covering condition assessment, original details, repair-versus-replace decisions and approval checks before work begins.
services.lead: Heritage timber work rewards careful observation. The best first decision is often to retain and repair sound original material rather than replace it by default.

sections.title: Record what is there before proposing a solution
sections.summary: Photograph each elevation and detail the parts that matter: profiles, mouldings, glazing bars, hardware, joints, paint build-up and areas of decay. Doors and windows may show localised damage at a sill, bottom rail or weather-exposed edge while much of the original joinery remains serviceable. A condition record helps distinguish a repairable component from one that has lost structural integrity.

sections.title: Repair, splice or replace: make the decision visible
sections.summary: A good repair scope states which timber is retained, which decayed sections are cut back, how new timber is matched and where joints will be placed. This makes it easier to compare a local splice, a rebuilt sash or a complete replacement. Matching the visual profile is important, but so are the water-shedding detail, glazing, fixing method and paint system that will protect the work after installation.

sections.title: Check heritage and planning requirements early
sections.summary: Some Adelaide properties are subject to heritage or planning controls. Requirements vary with the property and the proposed work, especially where external fabric or visible street-facing elements are affected. Contact MEL ONE for an on-site assessment of the heritage timber. We review the proposed repair, identify the heritage or planning requirements, and confirm qualified service arrangements and required project documents before work starts. Formal approvals remain with the relevant authority; this guide does not replace heritage or legal advice.

sections.title: Give the repair a maintenance plan
sections.summary: Timber lasts longer when paint failure, failed sealant, blocked drainage paths and exposed end grain are addressed early. At handover, ask what has been repaired, which finish system has been used, when it should be reviewed and which warning signs—such as cracking, sticking, water entry or soft timber—should prompt another inspection.

sections.title: Trace water before replacing timber
sections.summary: Decay around a sill, bottom rail or weatherboard junction commonly has a water-management story behind it. Observe flashing, drainage, end grain, paint failure, seals and the way the opening meets surrounding masonry or cladding. Replacing timber without resolving those interfaces can repeat the same damage cycle, even where the new work looks sound on the day it is installed.

sections.title: Respect evidence of the original construction
sections.summary: Old hardware, profiles, glazing bars, joints and paint layers can help explain how an element was built and what makes it visually significant. Recording those details before removal creates a better basis for repair or replication. It also allows owners, designers and heritage advisers to discuss a proposed change using evidence rather than a guess based on a modern equivalent.

sections.title: Scope concealed-condition risk honestly
sections.summary: External joinery can conceal deterioration behind paint, trims or internal linings. MEL ONE checks the accessible timber on site and agrees any careful opening-up needed to identify the damage. If hidden decay is found, we explain the additional repair and agree the scope and quote with you before proceeding.

sections.title: Coordinate paint, glazing and hardware
sections.summary: A repaired timber window or door depends on more than its joinery. Glazing, putty or sealant, hardware adjustment, paint preparation and final coating need to follow an appropriate sequence. Clarifying those interfaces early prevents a repaired sash or door from being installed without the finishing work required to protect it from weather and daily use.

sections.title: Build a staged restoration plan
sections.summary: For a larger Adelaide property, the best route may be to prioritise the most exposed or unsafe openings first, then schedule the remaining work over time. A condition record, photo set and agreed repair approach make that staging more consistent. It helps owners protect important fabric while planning budgets, approvals and access in a calm, evidence-led way.

insights.title: Why a full-spectrum carpentry partner is the smarter choice
insights.summary: Site carpentry and fine joinery look like two trades, but when one project splits them the cost is rework, delay and over-budget. Here is how a full-spectrum partner removes that pain.
insights.lead: Choosing a provider that runs both on-site carpentry and workshop joinery sharply cuts project risk and communication cost.

sections.title: The problem with split trades
sections.summary: Framing, fix-out and cabinetry by different subcontractors means mismatched measurements, poor sequence handover and rework cost that usually lands on the owner.

sections.title: The full-spectrum advantage
sections.summary: One team does frame measuring and cabinetry detailing, so dimensions line up; accountability is clear with no finger-pointing; program is coordinated and predictable.

sections.title: How to spot a true full-spectrum partner
sections.summary: Signs: ① own workshop and equipment; ② own site carpentry crew; ③ one complete quote (not piecemeal); ④ reference projects you can visit.

sections.title: Where coordination usually breaks down
sections.summary: The high-risk moments are rarely dramatic: a wall is lined before a niche is measured, a benchtop is ordered before services are set, or a door swing conflicts with a cabinet installed later. These gaps occur when each trade works from a different assumption. A coordinated carpentry and joinery process makes the interfaces visible before they become site fixes.

sections.title: One measure does not mean one guess
sections.summary: Integrated delivery is not about taking a single measurement and hoping it survives the build. It means revisiting critical dimensions at the right stage, documenting changes and deciding when workshop production should begin. Site conditions, linings, floor finishes and services can all affect the final fit, so the sequence matters as much as the initial design.

sections.title: How to compare scopes, not just totals
sections.summary: When comparing quotes, look for who owns set-out, site measure, shop drawings, material selection, protection, installation, adjustments and handover. A low initial figure may exclude the coordination that makes a complex room fit together. A useful quote names assumptions and interfaces so the owner can see what must be resolved before work starts.

sections.title: A practical project workflow
sections.summary: For a renovation or new build, the process normally moves from brief and drawings to site verification, detail decisions, production timing, staged installation and final adjustment. Not every project needs a large formal programme, but every project benefits from agreeing who makes decisions, when dimensions are confirmed and how late changes will be managed.

sections.title: Questions to ask before appointing a team
sections.summary: Ask what work is completed in-house, who will be your site contact, how measurements are verified, when custom pieces are released for manufacture and how defects or changes are handled. Clear answers demonstrate process knowledge. They are more informative than broad claims about quality because they show how a team protects quality under real project conditions.

insights.title: Adelaide kitchen renovation costs: 2026 market guide
insights.summary: A kitchen reno is among the highest-return home improvements. We lay out typical Adelaide 2026 price bands and the key cost drivers so you are not over- or under-quoted.
insights.lead: Compare the scope, materials and allowances clearly before choosing a quote. This Adelaide guide provides a practical starting point for planning.

sections.title: Typical Adelaide bands (2026)
sections.summary: Cosmetic (new doors + benchtop): $15,000–$30,000. Mid (full cabinets + new stone + tile): $30,000–$55,000. High (solid-timber + stone + appliances): $55,000–$100,000+.

sections.title: Five cost drivers
sections.summary: ① Cabinet material (solid > 2-pac > moisture board); ② Benchtop (natural stone > engineered > laminate); ③ Moving plumbing/power; ④ Demolition; ⑤ Project size (partial vs full strip).

sections.title: Holding the budget
sections.summary: ① Keep existing plumbing points (one move ~$500–800); ② Engineered stone is ~half natural stone, similar durability; ③ Replace doors only, keep boxes; ④ Avoid structural changes.

sections.title: Treat guide prices as a starting point
sections.summary: Our published kitchen price bands help you plan the work. MEL ONE measures the room, checks access and existing conditions, and confirms cabinetry, benchtops, appliances, services and finishes in the written quote. We discuss material choices and custom details so you can see what is included.

sections.title: Decide what must stay and what can move
sections.summary: Keeping plumbing, waste and major electrical points can simplify a renovation, but it should not override a layout that fails the household. Start with the non-negotiables: cooking workflow, storage, access, appliance positions and circulation. Then identify which changes add genuine daily value and which are aesthetic moves that can be deferred or achieved another way.

sections.title: Specify the joinery before selecting finishes
sections.summary: Cabinet depth, drawer configuration, appliance clearances, door style, handle detail and internal storage affect both cost and usability. Finish samples are important, but they should follow a layout that works. A client who understands the cabinet construction and hardware choices can compare alternatives more clearly than one choosing colour first and discovering functional compromises later.

sections.title: Plan the trade sequence
sections.summary: A kitchen renovation often involves demolition, rough-in services, wall and floor preparation, cabinetry installation, benchtop templating, splashback work, appliance connection and final adjustment. The exact order depends on the project. Identifying who owns each handover helps prevent a finished cabinet being removed or altered because a service or surface was not ready.

sections.title: Bring a quote-ready brief
sections.summary: Useful inputs include a plan or measured sketch, photos, appliance models, a list of storage priorities, preferred materials, the condition of the existing room and a target program. Note whether the project is occupied and whether other renovation work is planned. This helps create a scope that reflects the kitchen you need, not a generic package built around assumptions.

insights.title: Heritage timber restoration: how it differs from ordinary renovation
insights.summary: Heritage timber repair combines skilled craftsmanship with careful planning and preservation requirements. Learn why it needs a specialist team and what SA considerations may apply.
insights.lead: Many 1920–1950s Adelaide homes use traditional timber and hand joinery. Restoring them takes both skill and heritage awareness.

sections.title: Heritage listing and the rules
sections.summary: In SA, buildings on the State or Local Heritage Register need Heritage Approval (Section 49 permit) with a heritage-architect-reviewed method before timber repair starts.

sections.title: Traditional joinery demands
sections.summary: Mortise-and-tenon needs hand work not modern connectors; timber must match the original species and era; surface systems must follow period paint (lime wash, milk paint).

sections.title: MEL ONE heritage experience
sections.summary: Our joiners know Adelaide period forms (Federation Bungalow, Inter-War Californian Bungalow) and deliver compliant, faithful restoration.

sections.title: Start with significance, condition and use
sections.summary: Heritage timber work is strongest when three questions are considered together: what is significant about the existing fabric, what condition is it in, and what does the building need to do today? A visible original window may have heritage value even when it needs careful repair for weathering or operation. The answer is rarely a simple choice between untouched and replaced.

sections.title: Use evidence before making a replica
sections.summary: Profiles, surviving sections, old photographs, hardware and adjacent examples can all inform a repair or replacement detail. Recording these references before dismantling helps avoid a generic modern interpretation. Where a precise match is not possible, the proposed difference should be discussed openly with the project team and any relevant heritage adviser, not concealed by vague language.

sections.title: Plan moisture management as part of restoration
sections.summary: Timber does not fail in isolation. Flashing, drainage, glazing, paint, sealants, ventilation and adjacent masonry can all influence the service life of a repaired element. A restoration scope should identify these interfaces and the trades involved. This protects both the historic material that remains and the new timber introduced as part of a careful repair.

sections.title: Know when specialist advice is needed
sections.summary: MEL ONE assesses the heritage timber on site, records its condition and plans the repair with the approved project information. We identify structural, glazing, moisture, lead-paint and heritage requirements and confirm the qualified service arrangements and required documents before work starts. Contact our Adelaide team to arrange an assessment and quote.

sections.title: Create a maintainable handover record
sections.summary: Keep photos, notes on retained and replaced elements, material or finish information, and a simple schedule for review. This record gives future owners or trades a clearer picture of what was repaired and why. Heritage stewardship is easier when maintenance is based on evidence rather than a cycle of reacting only after paint failure, water entry or decay becomes obvious.

insights.title: Solid vs engineered timber flooring: which suits your home?
insights.summary: Solid and engineered timber each have trade-offs. The right pick balances budget, floor level, moisture and look.
insights.lead: Timber flooring is among the most-used surfaces in a home. The wrong choice costs heavily in repair; the right one lifts comfort and value.

sections.title: Solid timber pros & cons
sections.summary: Pros: natural grain, multiple sandings (100-year life), value. Cons: dearer, moisture-sensitive, pro install, not ideal on damp ground floors.

sections.title: Engineered timber pros & cons
sections.summary: Pros: ~60–70% of solid price, stable (less movement), straight onto slab, DIY-able. Cons: limited refinish (1–2 times), less warm sound.

sections.title: Adelaide recommendation
sections.summary: Ground floor: engineered (stable in moisture). Upper floors: budget-dependent. High budget + long value: solid (Blackwood, Jarrah). Wet areas (bath, laundry): hybrid flooring instead.

sections.title: Read the existing floor and subfloor first
sections.summary: A flooring choice is only as sound as the surface beneath it. Before selecting solid or engineered timber, understand slab or subfloor condition, flatness, moisture history, access, acoustic expectations and transitions to adjacent rooms. These factors affect preparation, installation method and long-term movement more than a showroom sample can reveal.

sections.title: Choose for the room, not the trend
sections.summary: A sunny living room, upper-level bedroom, entry, apartment and renovation over an existing slab place different demands on timber flooring. Consider traffic, pets, direct light, furniture, cleaning habits and the desired feel underfoot. The most suitable product is the one whose visual character, maintenance needs and installation conditions all match the room’s real use.

sections.title: Understand movement and visual variation
sections.summary: Timber is a natural material and can show grain, tone and seasonal movement. Board direction, width, feature grade, finish sheen and transition details influence how that variation reads across a room. Discussing samples and laying patterns early helps clients choose a look they will value over time rather than expecting every board to be identical.

sections.title: Plan edges, stairs and adjoining finishes
sections.summary: Flooring projects often become complicated at thresholds, fireplace surrounds, built-ins, stair nosings, skirtings and door clearances. These details deserve attention before the main field is installed. A clear plan for edges and transitions creates a more durable, finished result and prevents a small unresolved junction from holding up a larger room at the end.

sections.title: Care after installation
sections.summary: The right cleaning method, furniture protection, prompt attention to spills and sensible use of mats can help preserve a timber floor. Care advice should match the selected product and finish, not rely on a generic rule. Ask what to avoid, how to treat minor wear and when a professional review is appropriate so maintenance becomes planned rather than reactive.

insights.title: Commercial fitout, step by step: from design to opening
insights.summary: Restaurant, café, office or retail timber fitout is a complex job of design, fire and code compliance and program. Here is the full flow and key timing.
insights.lead: A well-planned fitout protects opening timelines, budget control and brand presentation. Understand the process before work begins.

sections.title: Stage 1 — Design & partners
sections.summary: Engage designer/architect → our joinery team details → coordinate fire engineer → submit DA (with heritage approval if needed). Typically 4–8 weeks.

sections.title: Stage 2 — Build & install
sections.summary: Workshop build (6–8 wks) → strip-out & base works → joinery install (2–3 wks) → paint/finish → hardware. Typically 8–12 weeks.

sections.title: Stage 3 — Handover & open
sections.summary: Building compliance → fire inspection → (food) health inspection → pre-open clean → soft furnishings. Usually 2–3 weeks after joinery.

sections.title: Timeline summary
sections.summary: Total ~16–26 weeks (4–6 months). A full fitout with DA is 2–3× a home job; start planning 6+ months out.

sections.title: Confirm the base building information
sections.summary: Before a fitout programme is treated as fixed, confirm the lease or landlord requirements, existing services, base-build condition, access rules and the approvals pathway. A beautiful concept can still stall if the site cannot receive materials, a service route is unavailable or a required approval has not been allowed for. Early information protects the opening date.

sections.title: Coordinate joinery with services
sections.summary: Counters, ceilings, partitions and feature walls commonly meet power, data, mechanical, hydraulic and fire services. The fitout team needs a shared view of where those interfaces occur and when they are checked. This is why shop drawings, site dimensions and trade coordination matter: they turn a visual layout into a buildable one without last-minute cutting into finished work.

sections.title: Separate critical path from nice-to-have items
sections.summary: Some decisions affect every following trade: layout, approvals, long-lead materials, services and core joinery dimensions. Others—such as movable furniture or minor decorative items—can often be resolved later. Identifying the critical path helps owners direct their attention where it has the greatest program value and reduces the chance that a late aesthetic choice delays essential construction.

sections.title: Protect quality under programme pressure
sections.summary: A fast commercial programme should not mean hiding decisions. Confirm finishes, access, tolerance, protection and handover responsibilities in writing, then review work at practical hold points. Clear records and a single point of contact make it easier to resolve issues while materials and trades are on site, rather than discovering them during final cleaning or the first week of trading.

sections.title: Prepare an opening-ready brief
sections.summary: Tell MEL ONE the intended opening date, tenancy or landlord arrangements, brand requirements, operating hours and nominated trades or suppliers. Existing drawings and site photos are optional for the initial request; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. We inspect and measure the premises, review known constraints and confirm the work, programme and quote. Required approvals and agreed specifications must be in place before the affected fitout work begins.

faqs.answer: Yes. MEL ONE holds a South Australian Building Work Contractor Licence issued by Consumer and Business Services (CBS). Our structural carpentry is carried out within licence scope and to the SA Building Rules.

faqs.question: Do you work with builders?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. We support house-and-land builders (carpentry subcontracting), renovation builders (kitchen/bath cabinetry supply and install) and commercial builders (fitout, formwork). We know AS 1684 framing and mainstream Australian build systems and slot into builder teams seamlessly.

faqs.question: What does custom cabinetry cost?
faqs.answer: Price depends on material, size and detail. MEL ONE cabinetry price range (cabinets only, no benchtops): standard 2-pac MDF $8,000–$18,000; mid composite $15,000–$30,000; solid/high-end (Blackwood, American Oak) $30,000–$60,000+. We give a written quote after measure, with a free preliminary assessment and 3D design.

faqs.question: Do you give free quotes?
faqs.answer: Yes — a free preliminary assessment and quote. Simple jobs (one furniture piece, small repair) get a phone/photo estimate; complex jobs (kitchen reno, structural carpentry, commercial fitout) get an on-site measure and a detailed written quote valid 30 days.

faqs.question: What does termite damage repair cost?
faqs.answer: Depends on extent and whether structure is involved: local jamb/floor replace $1,500–$5,000; partial frame repair (1–2 nodes) $5,000–$15,000; wide frame replace + barrier $15,000–$50,000+; engineer's report adds $1,500–$3,000. Act early — we coordinate a licensed pest controller to limit spread.

faqs.question: Can you do heritage building restoration?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our joiners know Adelaide period forms (Federation Bungalow, Inter-War Californian Bungalow, Georgian/Victorian) and their timber character and repair craft. For heritage-listed buildings we prepare a compliant method under the SA Heritage Act and obtain Heritage Approval before work.

faqs.question: How long from kitchen measure to install?
faqs.answer: Full kitchen reno (measure to install): standard cabinetry build 6–8 weeks; strip-out & base 1–2 weeks; install 1–2 weeks; finish & tune 3–5 days — about 10–14 weeks. Solid-timber cabinets may take 14–18 weeks for material lead. We give a dated program with clear milestones.

faqs.question: Do you take on commercial fitouts?
faqs.answer: Yes. We deliver timber fitouts for Adelaide venues (restaurants, cafés, bars — partitions, feature ceilings, bars, displays), offices (partition walls, meeting feature walls, reception) and retail (brand walls, custom furniture), plus hotels and clinics. On large jobs we work with the head contractor as carpentry subcontractor.

faqs.question: Can I see completed projects?
faqs.answer: Yes. With client consent we publish case studies (photos + description) on our projects page. For a specific type (kitchen, heritage, commercial fitout) we can arrange a visit where possible — Adelaide-local clients first.

faqs.question: How long for custom solid-timber furniture (e.g. a dining table)?
faqs.answer: Design sign-off 1–2 weeks; timber sourcing/drying (if specific size/species) 2–4 weeks; machining & assembly 2–3 weeks; finish (sand, oil/paint) 1 week — about 6–10 weeks. Local Blackwood/Jarrah can run longer on supply; imported Oak is usually quicker. Confirmed at quote.

faqs.question: What warranty and quality assurance do you provide?
faqs.answer: Structural carpentry: 6-year structural warranty per SA building law. Fine joinery/cabinetry: 2-year workmanship & material warranty. Floor & deck oiling: 1-year workmanship. Restoration: 1-year workmanship. All cover workmanship defects; material faults follow each supplier's warranty. Full terms are in the contract.

faqs.question: How do you manage site safety and cleanliness?
faqs.answer: We run SWMS (Safe Work Method Statement): site risk assessment before start; barrier and signage; daily site clean; waste sorted and removed at completion; all workers hold White Card + insurance. On commercial fitouts we coordinate hours (after-hours/weekends) with the head contractor to minimise trading disruption.

faqs.answer: Three ways: ① the contact form on our Contact page; ② phone 0403 202 949; ③ email handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com. We reply within 24 hours. When booking, please note project type (kitchen reno / new home framing / decking / heritage repair), suburb, rough budget and preferred start — so we send the right person.

about.process_lead: The responsible person, scope, access and booking arrangements should be understandable before a project moves from enquiry to site work.

process_steps.heading: Start with the property and the job
process_steps.body: Tell MEL ONE the Adelaide suburb, requested work, preferred timing and any access details. Existing photos, a room plan or drawings are optional for the first enquiry; email them to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com if available. We arrange the site measure or inspection and confirm any approved drawings or technical documents needed before work begins.

process_steps.heading: Identify specialist work early
process_steps.body: Carpentry often meets plumbing, electrical, waterproofing, glazing, engineering, heritage or other specialist work. MEL ONE confirms the qualified service arrangements, responsible contracting party, scope and required documents before that work is booked.

process_steps.heading: Agree the working scope
process_steps.body: Before work begins, confirm the intended outcome, inclusions, assumptions, timing, access, selected materials and any decision points. This gives homeowners and project teams a practical record to work from when site conditions or design decisions need attention.

about.priorities_title: What shapes a workable Adelaide project
about.priorities_lead: Existing conditions, everyday use and trade sequencing matter as much as the visible finish. Discussing them early leads to more durable decisions.

priorities.heading: Living or trading in the property
priorities.body: Access, dust, noise, pets, parking and rooms that must stay operational influence the practical staging of a home, tenancy or commercial project. Those details should be part of the initial brief, not an afterthought once materials arrive.

priorities.heading: Existing conditions
priorities.body: Older alterations, uneven walls, concealed services, moisture paths and prior repairs can affect the work. Contact MEL ONE to arrange an on-site assessment, identify the cause and confirm the repair plan and quote. We agree any further access or staged work with you before proceeding.

priorities.heading: Selections and lead times
priorities.body: Cabinetry, hardware, timber, glazing, flooring and made-to-order materials need to align with the project sequence. Selecting a finish is more useful when the dimensions, interfaces, installation access and timing are also understood.

faqs.question: Who is the contact for an Adelaide enquiry?
faqs.answer: Contact MEL ONE on 0403 202 949 or handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com. Include the suburb and a short description to arrange a site assessment. We inspect repairs or measure for new work and confirm the agreed scope and written quote. Photos are optional; email existing images to handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com.

faqs.question: Who completes specialist or regulated work?
faqs.answer: MEL ONE confirms qualified service arrangements, the relevant work scope and required documents before specialist, licensed, engineering, approval or certification work is booked. This helps clients understand what sits within the carpentry package and what is coordinated with another trade or professional.

faqs.question: Where does MEL ONE take enquiries?
faqs.answer: MEL ONE provides carpentry, joinery, maintenance and renovation services across Adelaide. Share the suburb and job details so we can confirm the assessment appointment, access and attending team, then provide the agreed scope and quote.

faqs.question: What information helps prepare a clear quote?
faqs.answer: Photos, drawings or dimensions, intended outcome, approximate timing, access constraints, existing conditions and any materials or appliances already selected are all useful. A good brief allows the conversation to focus on the real work required rather than a vague allowance that may not match the property.
